records.summary: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. records.summary: After the release of Grand Theft Auto VI this week, Rockstar employees like me can make history again. We need union recognition to safeguard our jobs When I first got the call offering me a job at Rockstar, I was thrilled. I thought back to being a child and sneaking into my brother’s room to grab the PlayStation Portable so I could secretly play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories. The same kid who fell in love with Rockstar’s games back then now gets to spend every day helping to create those worlds as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh. This week, we will celebrate the culmination of more than a decade of effort: the release of the most anticipated game of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI . But our team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month. Right now, the ballot is open for Rockstar employees to decide whether we want the union we have built with our colleagues to get recognition. As someone who cares deeply about our team, cares about what we do, and wants us to be able to keep delivering world-class games into the future, I’m voting yes. Continue reading...

It was “very moving”, says Gainsbourg to see her mother, the actor Jane Birkin, in 1972, “looking beautiful and in the middle of a demonstration”. At that time, in a court in Bobigny, a Paris suburb, the prominent lawyer Gisèle Halimi was defending 16-year-old Marie-Claire Chevalier, as well as her mother and two other women who helped her have an abortion, then illegal in France. The Bobigny trial was new to her, says Gainsbourg, who plays Halimi, a leading figure in French feminism and activism who died in 2020. “I had no idea. Charles (1938–2010) was unable to play an instrument yet wrote songs sung by everyone from Fats Domino to Etta James to Kris Kristofferson. Signed to Chess Records in 1955 aged 17, he was on the verge of becoming a star at the dawn of rock’n’roll, but a preference for living reclusively – with a pet alligator – ensured he vanished from sight, and his music has long been unavailable. “He was a very strange guy, a loner,” says one of his Louisiana contemporaries, 88-year-old Johnnie Allan. “He knew what he had and wouldn’t compromise.” Now a box set, The Bobby Charles Story, containing almost every recording Charles released, aims to establish the Cajun magus as one of the greats. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start. If you had been spying on me playing this game over the past few weeks you may well have caught me robbing banks, shooting up a weed farm or tearing along the highway at sunset blaring Bad Bunny on the in-game radio, but you might equally have caught me doing squats at the gym, shopping, assembling a coffee table or walking along the beach eating ice-cream. There is such a multiplicity of things on offer here that it is difficult to nail down what this game definitively is. Is it an interactive crime movie? A city simulator? A driving game? A sort of absurdly expansive version of The Sims in which the people you’re dressing up and looking after just happen to be professional criminals? It will be different for everyone – that is the beauty of it. For me, though, this game is about Jason and Lucia, the fugitive couple through whom you experience all that Leonida has to offer. records.title: ‘We want our story to be told’: inside a shocking 36-year fight for justice in Baltimore
records.summary: A staggering case of injustice is explored in the galling HBO documentary When a Witness Recants. The three subjects and producer Ta-Nehisi Coates explain how it unfolded For most of his life, the writer Ta-Nehisi Coates would occasionally think of a chilling episode from his childhood in West Baltimore: almost exactly 43 years ago, on 18 November 1983, a 14-year-old boy named DeWitt Duckett was shot and killed in a hallway of Harlem Park junior high school in the middle of the afternoon, by an older teenager who stole his blue satin Georgetown jacket. Coates was only eight years old at the time, too young to know the details, but old enough to perceive the collective horror around him. The sensational event – the first time a kid was killed inside a Baltimore public school, according to wall-to-wall local press – was a rupture in his child’s view of the world. “It was first time I had the sense that, oh, actually, I exist in a very dangerous world,” he told the Guardian. “And then you cut to the TV and it’s clear the rest of America is not existing in that dangerous world. The dangerous world is only for you and people who look like you.” Coates always assumed that the three teenage boys arrested and convicted for the murder were the right guys, and the episode faded into one of those strange imprints from the past, a blurry but foundational event. records.title: Gjak by Dimosthenis Papamarkos review – sensational tales of wartime Greek struggle
records.summary: Translated into English in thrilling style, these interlinked stories of ambushes and vendettas vividly evoke the bitter conflict of the 1919-22 Greco-Turkish war Nine interconnected tales about the violence of the 1919-22 Greco-Turkish war, and the struggles of its broken soldiers to reassimilate into civilian life, Gjak is something of a sensation. Originally written in Greek and Arvanitic, a dialect spoken by a Greco-Albanian ethnic group, and featuring characters from an unspecified Arvanite village, it was a hit in Greece in 2014 and comes to the UK in an agile translation by Siân Valvis. In her fascinating introductory note, Valvis writes of her attempt to capture the “unruly, galloping force” of Dimosthenis Papamarkos’s prose. She succeeds in thrilling style. Delivered in a demotic, gossipy voice, these are rough-hewn stories of ambushes and vendettas, of brothers in arms being “closer than kin” and of lingering, sour regret. One of the translations of the eponymous Arvanitic word “ gjak ” is “blood” and indeed, graphic bloodiness is inescapable. My mum used to leave out the last bit of lamb madras, with a wink, then loudly announce that she was going to bed. I have accidentally found myself in KFC at midnight, hood up, drunk, looking both ways and asking for a Bargain Bucket. My partner once came home early from a night out and caught me red-handed, in bed with McDonald’s Chicken Selects. Such incidents were infrequent moments of weakness and, after the fact, I was always racked with guilt. But for most of my vegetarian life, I had felt a certain emptiness; a gaping meat-shaped hole in my heart and stomach. Then I ate a bowl of pasta. records.title: The Limits Of Control: Why Human Nature Will Defeat China's AI Socialism
records.summary: The Limits Of Control: Why Human Nature Will Defeat China's AI Socialism Authored by Stu Cvrk via The Epoch Times , Beijing is betting that artificial intelligence (AI) can do what Gosplan never could : see everything, predict everything, and steer 1.4 billion people without the information failures that sank Soviet planning. The bet will probably make the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) better at control than any regime before it. But it will not make socialism work. The flaw in every planned society was never a shortage of data. It was human nature: people lie to those who watch them, officials protect themselves, and nobody can be ordered to care. AI does not cure those problems. It inherits them, scales them, and hides them behind a dashboard. The Machine in Brief The control apparatus already in place is vast. Some 600 million to 700 million cameras feed municipal "city brain" platforms that use face and gait recognition and flag crowds. Grid workers and volunteer informants watch neighborhoods of a few hundred households each. Blacklists bar "untrustworthy" people from planes, trains, and loans. Contrary to Western myth, though, there is still no single national personal score.

records.summary: China Turns To Iraqi Oil As US Blockade Chokes Iranian Supply Authored by Irina Slav via OilPrice.com , Chinese independent refiners are seeking crude oil cargoes from Iraq using the services of global commodity trading houses in a departure from their usual oil-sourcing practices, Bloomberg has reported, noting the continued U.S. blockade on Iranian ports. The malicious code rode in through Optimizely, a platform companies use to try out changes to their websites. records.title: NI Water Works - Cornagrade Road Enniskillen 3 Aug
records.summary: Essential Water Infrastructure Improvement Work gets underway – Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen NI Water is set to commence an upgrade of the water infrastructure on Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen in early August for approximately 6 weeks. The work will see around 400m of new watermain being laid along Cornagrade Road, starting at Cherrymount Roundabout on Monday 3 rd August and progressing as far as the second entrance to Kilmacormick Road. To facilitate the laying of this new watermain, a lane closure will be in place around each working area and signage will be in place. Working areas will be kept as short as possible (around 100m) with temporary traffic lights in place to manage the flow of traffic. Access to residential and business properties on and adjacent to Cornagrade Road will be available at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be affected for a short period of time while the pipelaying passes. Any bus stop located within a working area will be temporarily relocated.

records.title: Derry - NIW Scheme - Racecourse Rd - from 27 July
records.summary: Essential water network upgrade to get underway on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett NI Water is set to begin an essential watermain upgrade on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett (Derry/Londonderry) on Monday 27 th July to improve the resilience of the local water supply network. The work, which involves laying around 170 metres of new watermain between Carnhill Roundabout and Greenhaw Road, will replace a section of the 50-year-old Ballyarnett Water Trunkmain which has been prone to bursts. The upgrade will help to protect homes from flooding, should a burst occur in the future, and provide improved access for NI Water maintenance. A l ane closure controlled by temporary traffic lights will be in place on Racecourse Road around the working area from Monday 27 th July for four weeks. A further two weeks of work will take place in the adjacent verge which will not require any traffic management. records.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take the decision to go to war seriously?
records.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. methodology.reliability: A official primary source/catalogue; B established newsroom or independent research; C specialist, advocacy or aggregator; D alternative commentary; E unverified social/community; U unclassified. Grade describes source class, not the truth of a specific claim.
methodology.confidence: Claim confidence is left unassessed unless an upstream collector supplies a numeric value. Source grade is not claim confidence.
methodology.corroboration: The six views reuse the existing archive. Similar stories, repeated posts, syndicated copy or multiple outlets quoting one origin are not independent corroboration. A human must inspect provenance.
methodology.geolocation: Location is shown only when supplied by the source or upstream archive. No location is inferred from a headline.
methodology.limits: This is open-source situational awareness, not intelligence agency coverage, an emergency warning service, a live market terminal or a verified threat assessment.
